chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام one day: “May I be sacrificed for you. I mentioned the family of so-and-so and the blessings in which they are, and I said: if this were for you, we would have lived with you.”

So he عليه السلام said: “Far from it, O Muʿallā. Indeed, by Allah, if that had been so, it would have been nothing but managing through the night, traveling through the day, wearing coarse clothing, and eating rough food.”
So that was kept away from us. Have you ever seen an injustice that Allah, the Exalted, turned into a blessing except this one?”

key_terms.ظُلَامَةً: an act of injustice or wrongful deprivation
key_terms.هَيْهَاتَ: an expression of remoteness or impossibility

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام describe being kept from political rule as a blessing despite the injustice?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explaining that worldly rule and outward prosperity are not a simple blessing for the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, because true authority would entail hardship, discipline, and austere living. He also indicates that being deprived of such rule, despite the injustice involved, became a form of relief and blessing in one respect.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Moalla Bin Khunays who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> one day, ‘May I be sacrificed to you<sup>asws</sup>! I remembered the family of so and so and what they are in from the Bounties, so I said, ‘If only that was for you<sup>asws</sup>, we would have lived with you<sup>asws</sup> (prosperously)’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Far be it, O Moalla! But, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, had it been that, it would not have been except for hard labour (of protection) at night and strenuous work by the day, and wearing the coarse, and eating the tasteless.

So that was Impeded from us<sup>asws</sup>. Have you ever seen a looted property Allah, the Most High, has turned into a blessing except this one (easy life for you while unjust Abbassids are in rule)?’
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from Mu‘alla ibn Khunays who has said the following.

“One day I said to abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), may Allah take my soul in service for your cause, I thought of the descendants of so and so (‘Abbasside) and the wealth they have at their disposal. Then I wished that had such wealth been at your disposal we would have lived with you prosperously.”

The Imam (a.s.) said, “Never O Mu‘alla, by Allah, had it been as you wished, there would have been nothing but hard labor of protections at nights and strenuous work during the days, coarse garments and tasteless food.
Thus, it is kept away from us. Have you ever seen a usurpation that Allah, the Most High, would cause to become a blessing except this?”
